summary: Iteration 6 — Added /app/backend/tests/test_me_schedule.py with 8 new tests in a single TestMeSchedule class (xdist loadscope-pinned) verifying that /api/auth/me now includes the employee `schedule` field. All 8 new tests pass. Full backend suite (67/67) passes serially — no iteration-5 regression. Verified: (1) org_owner /me → schedule is None; (2) employee /me with weekly_calendar 06:40→09:00 for all 7 days returns exact structure {mode, timezone, weekly_schedule with all 7 day keys, each {open:06:40, close:09:00}}; (3) employee /me with fixed_hours=6 returns exact schedule; (4) PATCH from any → fixed_hours=8 + fresh employee login → next /me reflects new value (no stale caching); (5) REGRESSION: sessions/start inside a wide open window covering NOW returns 200 with remaining_ms ≈ ms-until-close (±5s); (6) sessions/start before shift → 403 with 'shift starts at HH:MM'; (7) after shift → 403 'shift ended at HH:MM'; (8) off-day → 403 'not scheduled to work today'. Teardown resets employee schedule to {mode:'any'} and deletes the TEST_MeSchLagos_* office.

action_items: (Low) Optional: server-side invalidation of any cached user snapshot on schedule PATCH — currently /me hits Mongo each call which is fine, so this is only future-proofing if a cache is introduced.
(Low, carried over from iter-5) Consider per-file dedicated test employees to make -n 2 --dist loadscope fully deterministic across the four session-touching test files.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py::/me duplicates the response dict inline instead of reusing _shape_user(user_doc, org). Minor DRY nit — both paths agree today but future field additions (like `schedule`) must be updated in two places (which is exactly what this iteration required). Suggest: fetch the full user doc via db.users.find_one and delegate to _shape_user for a single source of truth.

models.py::UserPublic.schedule is typed as Optional[Dict] — a loose dict. Consider re-using the EmployeeSchedule Pydantic model for stronger client-side contracts (would auto-validate/normalize on serialization).

The `get_current_user` dependency (deps.py) likely re-reads the user from DB each request — good, so /me is always fresh. Confirmed empirically by test_me_reflects_new_schedule_after_patch_and_relogin. Just document this invariant so future perf work doesn't accidentally cache a stale user snapshot at token-decode time.

Carried from iter-5 (still valid): (a) _compute_schedule_duration_ms disallows overnight shifts (close_dt <= open_dt → 'Invalid schedule'), (b) EmployeeSchedule allows partial weekly_calendar (mode+timezone but no weekly_schedule) which _compute treats as universal off-day — add stricter validator, (c) bad IANA tz silently downgrades to UTC — should 422 at model boundary.
